name: teal_filaments
description: soft glowing teal Julia filaments and curl clusters in a dark green-grey mist: each cluster a pale aqua glow with a wide haze round it, soft broad bands of mist sweeping round the structure, no hot white core

reference.made_with: a Julia set render with glow and mist (signed exoteric.roach.org), 2560x1600

reuses: a literal dark green-grey ground (a glow at power near zero on de), under a dim fog of the inverted distance estimate through the map by rank at gamma 4
two wide falloff glows on de (8e-2 and 2e-2 frame widths) from the map's middle: the haze round each cluster

glow_filaments' falloff glows on de, softened: no hair-wide near-white add core, the innermost glow 4e-4 wide and screened from the map's middle, so dense lace stops at a mid tone instead of flooding white
field smooth as a period sheet with a scoop (fill 0.35, edge 0.12): soft broad bands of mist sweeping round the structure, where glow_filaments drew hair-thin equipotentials
the tone pass, at the reference's median and p10
notes: Round one's palette entries from item 045 (values in the catalog's set, unkept until a tile is): law_of_ice_glow (law-of-ice-25.jpg), an indigo-to-cyan map, a deep navy ground (layer 0), the de bands at 0.9 and the haze at 0.3 so the far field darkens to indigo, the glows read cyan from the map's upper half; it still misses p10 (0.39-0.59 against 0.21) and the near-white share (0.14 against 0.02): the tone pass lifts a frame whose only darks are the far field, and the reference's darks are its corners. holy_dark_glow (holy-dark-25.jpg), a blue-black to silver map with the wide haze lifted to the map's 0.7 so the clusters glow silver, tone 0.159/0.036; the reference's dense frame-filling texture is not reached by one Julia set's lace.
Added: nothing: `glow_filaments`' falloff glows softened, two wide haze glows and a scooped period sheet on the smooth count for the mist, on a literal ground

Lessons: The fifteenth to seventeenth styles came in one item, from three glow references built on `glow_filaments`: `teal_filaments` (soft teal curl clusters in a green-grey mist), `ember_rose` (a rose of layered petals in crimson, red-orange and gold, bead-studded, on black) and `star_eye` (a luminous blue ring round a star, strands radiating out). All three went in with **no new primitive**, and share one stack builder: a ground, a fog, softened falloff glows, a period sheet on the smooth count, and per style one more channel. Four lessons. **A soft thread is a mid-tone core, not a dim one**: `glow_filaments`' threads are hot because their innermost glow is a hair (2e-4) of the map's near-white top, added; screened from the map's middle at 4e-4 instead, dense curls stop at a pale aqua rather than flooding white. Dimming did nothing beyond that, as before: under a dark rank fog every teal draft read p90 ~0.85 against 0.666 whatever the glows' paints, because the tone pass lifts a dark ground with a curve that carries the structure to near-white. **The softness is the ground's**: a literal mid green-grey under a dim fog needs no such lift, and 36 of 40 teal drafts hold. **A rank fog always spends the map's top on the frame's nearest tenth**: `star_eye`'s ring drawn by the inverted distance by rank read p90 0.64–0.70 at most seats at any gamma or opacity, and dimming the other layers made it worse; a falloff glow (3e-2) for the ring over a quarter of the fog holds 27 of 40, every miss but one a view whose disc fills the frame. **A structure the galleries lack can be a family of Julia sets chosen for it**: the rose is a parabolic Julia set (`z^d + c` with a fixed point of multiplier `e^(2πi p/q)`, centred on it), whose basin's `inside` count cycled round the map draws petal rings layered about the parabolic point, and the eye is a quasicircle (`z^d + c` at small `c`) seen whole, where the `lines` channel inside the ring draws a star round the attracting fixed point. Narrow views of the flower read as a bullseye of polygons and views whose pupil is a flat disc read as one object, so both were dropped: **a frame must look as if zooming in would show more** (Matt's ruling). Parabolic seats are slow, since the whole basin iterates to the cap: a `--draft` took ~30 s at six threads at maxiter 3000, so their records carry maxiter 1000, which the `inside` channel's own 1000 already reads.
